A monsoon surge continues well to the south of Typhoon Dolphin, which
is currently centered east of Iwo To near 25N147E. Sustained west
winds and gusts picked up today as heavy showers and thunderstorms
developed across the Marianas, with sustained winds briefly reaching
28 mph at the Guam airport, and up to 20 mph on Saipan. These
conditions will continue into midweek, with a peak in winds 
anticipated Tuesday across the Marianas. Model guidance and 
observational trends indicate the highest winds will be felt over 
Guam and its coastal waters, and a Wind Advisory remains in effect
for Guam through early Wednesday morning, with sustained winds of 20
to 30 mph expected with gusts to around 40 mph, mainly near the
heaviest showers. Winds are expected to relax Wednesday night through
Friday as a col area develops just north of the region, but this is
dependent on the development and movement of a secondary, weak 
disturbance along the eastern extent of the monsoon trough, north of 
the Marshall Islands. Models depict an elongated circulation
beginning to develop somewhere near Wake Island on Tuesday, but as a
disturbance has not yet formed, uncertainty remains somewhat high in
the wind forecast toward the end of the week. Visible satellite 
imagery and CIMSS 850 mb vorticity analysis do show an area of low- 
level vorticity, co-located with developing convection to the north 
of Majuro. As a disturbance develops, uncertainty will decrease with 
regards to the regional pressure gradient and broader wind field.
Late this weekend into early next week, the monsoon pattern looks to
resurge across the Marianas, which will reinforce marine and surf
hazards, discussed below.

Marine/Surf...
Fresh to strong westerlies with near-gale to gale force gusts 
prevail across the Marianas through early Wednesday, especially near
heavier showers as a westerly monsoon surge continues. Additionally,
distant Typhoon Dolphin (12W) is generating a long- period north to 
northeast swell that is moving through the Marianas, which will 
continue shift north over the next day or so, then northwest. 
Meanwhile, the developing monsoon pattern will lead to increasing 
west to southwest swell over the coming days. The combination of 
these elevated swells and wind waves will keep seas at around 10 feet
across the coastal waters, maintaining hazardous sea conditions for 
much of this week. A Small Craft Advisory is currently in effect 
through early Friday morning.

Additionally, a High Risk of Rip Currents and High Surf Advisory are
in effect for north and east facing reefs of the Marianas. The high
rip current risk is expected to continue for north and east reefs for
the next few days, but as the long-period swell direction shifts
northerly, surf is expected to fall below hazardous levels of 12 feet
along east reefs Tuesday, remaining hazardous along north reefs. A 
high risk of rip currents and hazardous surf are then expected to 
develop along west facing reefs beginning Tuesday as monsoonal swells
strengthen. A moderate risk of lightning is expected through at least
midweek.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Dolphin (12W) was centered east of Iwo To near 25N148E at 
1:00 PM ChST. Dolphin is moving WNW at 12 mph. TY Dolphin continues
to slowly weaken, with maximum sustained winds now at 115 mph. 
Dolphin is expected to make a slight turn toward the west with a
slight increase in speed over the next couple of days. Dolphin will 
continue to approach Iwo To, with the current track showing Dolphin 
passing near or over the island within the next 36 hours. Residents 
should prepare for typhoon conditions. 

For more information on TY Dolphin please refer to bulletins issued
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and
by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Latest model guidance shows an overall dry pattern continuing over
eastern Micronesia for the next several days as the monsoon trough
remains well north of the area. Latest satellite data shows all of
the convection north of the forecast points, north of 10N from 
Pohnpei to Kosrae, then north of 8N over the Marshall Islands. As TY 
Dolphin continues to move toward Iwo To, it will drag the monsoon 
trough along with it, slightly farther north over the next few days. 
The monsoon trough may eventually break away from TY Dolphin, though 
this does not look likely into the weekend.

For the marine environment, the north swell will slowly subside over
the next few days as Dolphin moves farther west, though the trade- 
wind swell looks to build slightly. This will keep seas fairly
consistent through the week. Gentle to moderate wind at Pohnpei will
become light to gentle by the end of the week, with light to gentle
winds expected to continue across Pohnpei and Majuro into the
weekend.
